title: NovusBank integration call notes - SLA & deployment
content:
Meeting: NovusBank integration sync (call notes, requirements, gotchas, next steps)
Date: 2026-02-18
Attendees: Alex Santos (Redwood CS), Priya Nair (Redwood AM), Jordan Kim (Redwood Solutions),
           Mark Rivera (NovusBank - Platform), Lena Wu (NovusBank - Security), Tom Bates (NovusBank - ML)

High-level summary:
- NovusBank evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Private for production inference (sensitive PII, regulatory).
- Primary goals: predictable latency (<150ms p99 for 1k token prompts), strict data residency (EU) and auditability, and clear cost model for forecasting.
- They currently run ModelServeX for some workloads; want to migrate customer-facing assistants and embeddings pipeline.

Customer requirements (explicit):
- Deployment: Private control plane with VPC peering into their EU region (Ireland). On-prem is optional for later.
- Networking: static egress IPs or small range for allowlisting; must work through bank firewall.
- Data: request/response logs must be configurable (keep/no-logs) and support customer-managed KMS for key rotation.
- SLA: 99.95% uptime target for production endpoints; latency SLOs: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 120ms, p99 < 150ms for standard prompts (avg 800 tokens).
- Throughput: initial steady-state ~50 qps for chat endpoints, burst to 200 qps during peak. Embeddings ~20 qps (smaller token sizes).
- Model variants: want to run two model classes: cost-optimized (quantized 4/8-bit) for low-cost bulk responses, and high-quality variant (FP16) for fraud detection workflows.
- Fallback: automatic fallback policy required (if Dedicated capacity exhausted, route to pre-approved hosted model variant in EU with strict logging off).
- Compliance: must produce audit logs per request and be able to demonstrate encryption at rest + in transit.

Notes / gotchas observed during call:
- NovusBank legal will push back on any logging that could retain customer PII; need clear per-route logging toggles and redaction guidance.
- They require a SOC2-type evidence pack + pen test schedule before go-live. Coordinate with security team.
- Static IP requirement is hard in shared cloud; likely need Dedicated with egress NAT or Private offering that supports fixed IPs — flag to infra.
- Billing & forecasting: they want predictable monthly costs — reserved capacity contract for Dedicated looks promising but they need example numbers for 50 qps baseline. Priya to prepare a modeled cost worksheet.
- Existing vendor (ModelServeX) has a custom batching mechanism that they like — need to compare batching behavior and how Redwood batching interacts with their request patterns.

Technical notes (to engineering):
- Estimate tokens per response: average prompt 400 tokens + generation 400 tokens => ~800 tokens per call. Embeddings ~256 tokens. Use these for cost modeling.
- Check GPU memory needs for model variants (esp. high-quality FP16). Might need multi-GPU sharding for the fraud detection model.
- Confirm KV cache behavior across private deployment (sticky sessions?) — Novus team worried about user context preservation and cold-start latencies.
- Routing: discuss policy to allow canary to hosted EU fallback with logging disabled. Need automated rollback if latency > 200ms for 5m window.

Action items / next steps:
- Priya: build a draft Dedicated reserved-capacity pricing sheet for NovusBank (include 50 qps baseline + 3x burst scenario) — due 2026-02-23.
- Jordan: reach out to infra + private-deployments to confirm static egress IP options and timeline for VPC peering (ASAP, target 2026-03-05).
- Alex (me): assemble compliance checklist (SOC2 evidence, pen-test cadence, KMS integration docs) and share with Lena — due 2026-02-22.
- Engineering (assigned): short tech write-up on batching and KV cache behavior in Private vs Dedicated, include expected p99 under cold-start and warm cache — tentative owner: @eng-serving-runtime — due 2026-02-27.
- Schedule next call: propose 2026-02-25 (bi-weekly sync cadence afterward). Alex to send Doodle.

Questions to resolve (follow-ups):
- Can Redwood provide static egress IPs on Dedicated in EU region or do we need Private on-prem? (Infra)
- What are the exact retention controls and redaction options for request/response logs? (Product/Security)
- Cost sensitivity: how flexible are they on quantized models vs FP16 for customer-facing chat? They want a quality guardrail. We should prepare quality delta notes. (Applied ML/Product)

Notes to self (informal):
- Follow up with Priya after she shares pricing sheet — have examples of similar banking customers to reference.
- Prep short demo of canary fallback (hosted EU) + log toggle to show during next call. Keep it simple.
- Confirm who on legal side will own contract language for data processing and KMS.

Raw chat snippets / partial quotes:
- Lena (Security): "We need to be able to prove we never store PII outside the bank-managed KMS."
- Mark (Platform): "If you can give us a predictable monthly invoice and an easy way to burst, we can move quickly."

End of notes.

-- alex
